title: Paloma and the Salt
premise: Ulyana Thackeray, last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, bottled storms, names not yet earned. When a mute child called Paloma arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ulyana discovers the boy is a living covenant — and that the dragon-fire sealing the pact between realms is guttering toward extinction. Hunted by her own guild, who would sell the covenant's terms to the highest bidder, Ulyana must choose between the oath that made her and the truth that unmakes it. In the end she reforges the covenant at terrible cost, surrendering her swordspeech to kindle the new flame, while Paloma, grown into his inheritance, becomes the bridge between realms.
about_author: Tamsin Fairweather is a former archivist from the Cornish coast who writes fantasy steeped in ledger-lore, salt air, and old bargains. Her short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies; 'Paloma and the Salt' is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A night of routine trade at the Salt Guild — a widow buys back one hour of her husband's voice — establishes the guild's rules and Ulyana's quiet, oath-bound loneliness. The emotional beat is controlled melancholy, ending when a knock comes at the door past closing.

chapters.title: A Boy Who Speaks Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The child Paloma arrives half-frozen, uttering words no living tongue should know — and every impossible thing in the guild's vaults resonates when he speaks. Ulyana hides him as the guildmaster's interest sharpens. Beat: reluctant protectiveness awakening.

chapters.title: What the Oath Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with an interlude of Paloma's fragmentary memories. Flashbacks reveal how Ulyana swore the swordspeaker's oath after her order was massacred for refusing to sell the covenant. The guildmaster demands she hand over the boy. Beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Grey Marshes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ulyana flees with Paloma through marsh country where traded things go to die — ghost-lanterns, unpaid debts given flesh. Pursued by guild hunters, she teaches him basic speech; he teaches her his first word. Beat: trust kindling under pressure.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They reach the drowned crater where the last dragon, Vessarion, sleeps coiled around the guttering covenant-flame. The dragon reveals Paloma is the covenant made flesh, and that the guild has been siphoning its fire for decades. Beat: awe curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Captured by the guild, Ulyana is offered everything she lost — her order restored, her name cleared — if she surrenders Paloma's heartfire to renew the guild's monopoly on impossibility. Beat: temptation, and love against duty crystallizing into refusal.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Ulyana burns the guild's master ledger, freeing every traded thing — including debts owed by the hunters themselves, who turn mid-siege. The guildmaster unleashes the hoarded fire. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the first open act of rebellion.

chapters.title: Where the Fire Gutters
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the crater, the covenant-flame shrinks to a coal as the guildmaster arrives with an army of bought loyalties. Vessarion offers Ulyana a choice: her swordspeech can reignite the flame, but the oath will take it forever. Beat: dread before the climax.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. Ulyana speaks her final sword-oath, pouring her gift into the flame while Paloma stands between armies, translating peace into the pre-kingdom tongue until even hired blades weep. The guildmaster falls into fire he cannot buy. Beat: triumph purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Salt in the Morning Air
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. A year later, the reformed guild keeps honest ledgers under new law; Vessarion sleeps easier, the flame steady. Ulyana, voiceless of magic but not of kindness, teaches children — and Paloma, growing into his role as living bridge, signs to her: home. Beat: bittersweet resolution.
